claims.text: In refractory high-entropy alloys, retention of toughness is governed by the formation and stability of coherent nanoprecipitates.
Dislocations can shear through coherent δ-lamellae and be pinned by γ″ particles.
Dislocation transmission and shearing across coherent precipitate interfaces can accommodate local shear and relieve stress concentrations that would otherwise promote premature crack initiation.
The coherent nanoprecipitate-mediated process prevents crack propagation.
A controlled thermal aging treatment can induce a targeted volume fraction and distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates in the tungsten-based refractory HEA.
The initial homogenized tungsten-based alloy is largely single-phase or contains only incoherent second phases without a controlled nanoprecipitate distribution.
Coherent δ-lamellae and γ-type nanoscale particles can occur as structural mediators in a tungsten-based refractory HEA.
Coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate planar dislocation slip and local shear accommodation.
Compared with the baseline state, the thermally aged alloy will have higher fracture toughness.
Compared with the baseline state, an alloy containing controlled coherent nanoprecipitates will have improved tensile ductility.
Tungsten-based refractory HEAs designed with SCCPs can exhibit 15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature and a yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 °C.
Toughness has a nonmonotonic dependence on precipitate density, with moderate density enhancing toughness while very low or overly high density produces suboptimal toughness.
The proposed toughness mechanism applies broadly to refractory-element HEAs with similar multiphase microstructures when dislocation-mediated plasticity dominates.
The behavior may differ when grain-boundary sliding is significant, such as in ultrafine-grained alloys.
The precipitate volume-fraction threshold and optimum required to maximize toughness are not established.
Excessive aging may cause secondary phase transformations that embrittle the alloy.

contradictions.description: The prediction allows overly high precipitate density to reduce toughness, but the falsification rule gives reduced toughness following increased precipitate density as an example that would falsify the hypothesis. Without a defined moderate or optimal density range, an observation of reduced toughness could be either predicted behavior or falsification.
